fig1_first_law_plane.svg: The closed-system first law $E_2-E_1=Q-W$ (delta_E) drawn over the whole $(Q,W)$ plane. Because it is linear, its contours are parallel lines at 45$^\circ$: any heat input can be matched by an equal work output with no change in stored energy. The highlighted $\Delta E=0$ contour is exactly the condition a cycle must satisfy, since a cycle returns the system to its initial state. Everything above that line drains the system's energy; everything below charges it.
fig2_power_cycle.svg: A cycle stores no energy, so the first law collapses to $W_{cycle}=Q_{cycle}$ (cycle_net_work) and a power cycle's net work is simply what it takes in minus what it throws away, $W=Q_{in}-Q_{out}$ (power_cycle_work). Supplying 1000 kJ while rejecting 400 kJ yields 600 kJ of work, and first_law_holds confirms the books balance. Nothing in the first law forbids the grey line $Q_{out}=0$ — a cycle converting heat entirely into work. Ruling it out takes the second law (module 3.3).
